title: A derivative predicts the next small step
alt: A parabola and its tangent at t=2. They meet with equal slope but differ away from the contact point.
caption: The tangent captures the value and first derivative. Curvature enters at the next order; the same hierarchy will appear in a local expansion of the metric.

title: One laboratory is not enough
alt: One worldline is compared with a pair of approaching free-fall worldlines, with time increasing upward.
caption: The paired experiment measures relative acceleration. Curved drawn paths are coordinate schematics; their appearance alone is not evidence of curvature.

title: A century of consequences
alt: Ten dated milestones progress from Newton’s Principia to the first direct gravitational-wave detection.
caption: Dates label selected developments, not a complete priority history. The 2015 LIGO event was publicly reported in 2016. The text discusses the collaborative and iterative development of the field equations.

title: Arrows and the questions they answer
alt: A diagonal vector crosses three evenly spaced level intervals of the function x.
caption: The covector dx returns the change in x, not the Euclidean length of the arrow. Changing the coordinate scale changes both components so their pairing stays the same.

title: The minus sign creates a light cone
alt: Two light rays bound the possible future of an event. A slower-than-light path lies inside, and a spacelike displacement lies outside.
caption: The graph uses the same scale for x and ct. A massive observer follows a timelike worldline; no rest frame exists for a light ray.

title: Two histories between the same events
alt: A home clock follows a vertical worldline for ten years. A traveller reaches three light-years in five years and returns in another five.
caption: The idealized travelling clock accumulates 10√(1 − 0.6²) = 8 years. The sharp turnaround is an approximation; the path integral, not a local feeling of slow time, gives the age difference.

title: Coordinates are not rulers
alt: A polar grid has an annular sector highlighted; its radial and angular edges have different measuring factors.
caption: For an infinitesimal cell, the angular edge is r dθ and the radial edge is dr. The finite cell is enlarged for visibility; the plane is intrinsically flat.

title: Why a determinant belongs in the volume
alt: A square transforms into a parallelogram under a linear map; the absolute determinant is its area scaling.
caption: This Euclidean two-dimensional example explains the square root of the metric determinant. In four-dimensional Lorentzian geometry the positive measure uses √(−g). The drawn transformation is illustrative.

title: Acceleration without curvature
alt: Three Rindler hyperbolae lie inside a lightlike asymptote in an inertial spacetime diagram.
caption: Each curve is a stationary rocket-frame observer. In a rigid accelerated laboratory, different heights require different proper accelerations. These worldlines occupy flat Minkowski spacetime.

title: Do not confuse a route with its parameter
alt: Two identical straight paths have respectively equally spaced and nonuniformly spaced parameter labels.
caption: This flat straight-line illustration isolates parameter choice. Affine parameters are related by λ ↦ aλ + b; an arbitrary nonlinear relabeling changes the standard coordinate form of the geodesic equation.

title: Different components can describe the same arrow
alt: At three points on a circle the eastward vector stays horizontal while radial and angular basis directions rotate.
caption: The ordinary component derivatives see changing numbers. The connection correction accounts for the basis change. Together they report that this field is constant.

title: The connection cancels a false change
alt: The partial derivative of the radial vector component is minus sine theta; its Christoffel correction is plus sine theta.
caption: This is an exact calculation on the flat polar plane. The derivative direction is θ. The full indexed equation in the chapter identifies the single connection coefficient used in this cancellation.

title: A sphere remembers the loop
alt: An orthographic spherical octant connects the north pole with two equatorial points ninety degrees apart. The returned tangent arrow differs from the initial arrow.
caption: Great-circle transport around this octant rotates a tangent vector by 90°. Projection changes apparent angles on the page; the right angles and 90° rotation are intrinsic to the sphere.

title: From 256 slots to 20 independent entries
alt: A six-by-six matrix of antisymmetric index pairs has one triangular half highlighted, representing twenty-one symmetric entries before Bianchi.
caption: Riemann antisymmetry creates six pair labels; pair-exchange symmetry leaves 21 entries. The algebraic Bianchi identity removes one in four dimensions. This counts local tensor components, not propagating gravitational degrees of freedom.

title: Volume and shape ask different questions
alt: An initial circular section is compared with a smaller circle and with a stretched ellipse.
caption: These are exaggerated cross-sections of infinitesimal clouds, not exact finite volume-preserving motions. The trace controls initial volume acceleration for an initially comoving cloud; shear can later change the volume.

title: Stretching and squeezing near Earth
alt: Radial particles accelerate apart; tangential particles accelerate toward one another. The three tidal acceleration eigenvalues sum to zero.
caption: The labels give eigenvalues of the Newtonian relative-acceleration matrix, not curvature components: divide by c² for the corresponding curvature scale, with the convention-dependent sign tracked in the text.

title: The source has more than one kind of entry
alt: A four-by-four stress-energy matrix colors energy density, mixed energy-momentum entries, and spatial stresses differently.
caption: S is energy flux, π is momentum density, and σ denotes the spatial stress entries using the momentum-flux convention. The tensor is symmetric in ordinary metric GR.

title: Read the equation as a relationship
alt: The colored Einstein equation connects violet curvature and a teal metric to amber stress–energy. The constants and index letters remain neutral.
caption: The equation constrains spacetime geometry and matter together. It is not a recipe that chooses arbitrary matter independently of its own dynamics and conservation.

title: Where the factor of eight comes from
alt: Geometry, the trace-reversed dust source, and Poisson’s equation combine to fix the coupling constant.
caption: The displayed component estimates assume weak, stationary fields and slow pressureless matter, with x⁰=ct. The matching is performed in the chapter with the full index conventions.

title: A derivative of whole paths
alt: Three curves share fixed initial and final positions; a smooth variation changes their interiors.
caption: A variation is a mathematical comparison with nearby candidate histories. The physical stationary path is found by requiring the first action change to vanish for every allowed variation.

title: Two variations make one field equation
alt: A two-branch flowchart separates the variation of scalar curvature from the variation of the invariant volume.
caption: The boundary divergence requires its own treatment. After that treatment, the bulk coefficient of the arbitrary inverse-metric variation is the Einstein tensor.

title: Fixing the value does not fix the slope
alt: A variation vanishes at both endpoints while having nonzero slopes there.
caption: The scalar graph is an analogy for each metric variation component along a normal direction. It explains why the Einstein–Hilbert action needs appropriate boundary treatment even when the boundary metric is fixed.

title: A symmetry supplies an energy comparison
alt: Repeated geometric slices are connected by a time-translation vector, next to the conserved pairing minus p dot xi.
caption: The drawing is schematic. A timelike Killing vector provides a stationary energy; normalization and the observer’s local energy measurement must still be specified.

title: A ray samples more than the clock rate
alt: A light ray bends toward a mass relative to its straight incoming reference line; the impact parameter is marked.
caption: This is the shape from a first-order weak-field deflection profile, with its amplitude enlarged. The book derives why keeping only the clock term misses half the leading GR deflection.

title: A slowly turning orbit
alt: Three aligned-focus ellipses have progressively rotated perihelia. Their offset is greatly exaggerated.
caption: The curves are schematic successive Kepler ellipses, compressed vertically for layout, not a numerical integration of an exact relativistic orbit. The text derives the small secular advance and states its regime.

title: Altitude and motion compete
alt: A net orbital-clock gain curve crosses zero near 3186 km and is positive at GPS altitude.
caption: Calculated for circular orbits around a nonrotating spherical Earth and compared with a stationary surface clock. Real GPS also models rotation, eccentricity, the geoid, and signal propagation.

title: The tossed clock records more time
alt: A parabolic height-time trajectory returns to the shelf after one second; its altitude and motion clock effects are compared.
caption: This calculation assumes uniform g, weak gravity, slow motion, and negligible launch/catch durations. The shelf clock and tossed clock share both comparison events.

title: Do not merge these three radii
alt: Three concentric circles have coordinate radii in the ratio two to three to six.
caption: Circle radii are proportional to the Schwarzschild areal coordinate r. The drawing is a radial coordinate guide, not an isometric picture of spatial proper distances.

title: A horizon changes which way the future goes
alt: At four radii, future radial light cones tilt inward. The outward generator is vertical at the horizon and points toward smaller radius inside.
caption: The diagram uses regular ingoing coordinates, not singular Schwarzschild time. Cone slopes follow dr/dT = −1 and (r − rₛ)/(r + rₛ). T is a drawing coordinate, not a freely falling clock reading.

title: Two independent patterns of strain
alt: Two test-particle rings are distorted into ellipses along axes separated by forty-five degrees.
caption: The figure shows a local detector-frame interpretation at one phase, to first order in strain. Real astrophysical strains at Earth are vastly smaller; the interactive figure lets you move through a cycle.

title: Expansion is not the same as acceleration
alt: Radiation and dust scale factors grow with downward curvature; a positive cosmological-constant model grows exponentially.
caption: Each ideal flat model is normalized to a(1)=1. The exponential curve uses H=2/3 in these plot units; it does not begin with a finite-time big bang in this slicing. These are separate single-component universes.

title: A causal horizon is not just a distance scale
alt: Past and future light rays in conformal coordinates meet initial and finite future boundaries.
caption: The diagram depicts a model with finite past and future conformal intervals. Their lengths determine particle and event horizons. Other expansion histories can lack one or both boundaries; c/H is a different construction.

title: Lapse and shift separate two choices
alt: A diagonal coordinate-time step is decomposed into a normal step between slices and a tangential shift.
caption: Lapse controls normal proper-time separation; shift controls the tangential relabeling. Arrow lengths are schematic and do not represent an ordinary Euclidean decomposition of a Lorentzian norm.

title: Two physical degrees of freedom, counted honestly
alt: Twelve initial-data functions lose four constraints and four gauge directions, leaving four phase-space functions.
caption: This is the local canonical count for ordinary four-dimensional GR, with first-class constraints. Four remaining phase-space functions describe two propagating configuration degrees of freedom.

title: Same method, different curvature
alt: Side-by-side coframe, connection, and curvature formulas compare the polar plane with the sphere.
caption: These are local formulas on regular angular charts. The polar origin and sphere poles need other frames; a singular coordinate expression there is not an extra curvature singularity.

title: Focusing is not yet a singularity
alt: Five straight timelike paths converge to a caustic, alongside the focusing time bound.
caption: This flat-spacetime schematic intentionally has no curvature. Raychaudhuri can force a congruence to focus, but singularity theorems require additional causal and global assumptions to conclude geodesic incompleteness.

title: Two areas constrain one remnant
alt: Two equal initial Schwarzschild horizons are compared with a limiting final circle whose area equals their sum.
caption: The equality illustration is the bound’s limiting case, not an achievable merger prediction. Initial binding energy is neglected, and all holes are assumed nonspinning; Kerr horizons require a different area formula.

title: The information question has a shape
alt: A schematic entropy curve rises and returns to zero, while a dashed comparison curve continues to rise.
caption: Axes are qualitative and the curves are not a quantitative evaporation solution. A final pure radiation state has zero fine-grained entropy for the whole radiation system; individual portions can remain mixed.

title: A theory has a resolution scale
alt: A scale axis progresses from long wavelengths with controlled corrections toward a cutoff with no small expansion parameter.
caption: This is a hierarchy diagram, not a measured error curve. The cutoff depends on the theory and physical setting; the text distinguishes gravitational scales from other possible new-physics scales.

title: From a metric to a measurement
alt: Six stages organize a general relativity calculation, from specifying the metric to checking physical limits.
caption: The observer can often be chosen earlier. This map is a practical organizing sequence; it is not a claim that every problem needs every tensor computed explicitly.
